title: [Feature Request]: Add Embedding Caching
body:
### Feature Description

To reduce redundant embedding computations, the `BaseEmbedding` class could be extended to accept an optional `BaseKVStore` parameter for embedding caching. This enhancement addresses concerns raised in issues #18840 and #18843, particularly regarding repeated query embedding computations in `NLSQLRetriever` and potentially other retriever classes.

Integrating this feature is straightforward: the query embedding methods — `get_query_embedding` and `aget_query_embedding` — can first check the cache before performing embedding computation.

### Reason

In certain cases—such as in the `NLSQLRetriever` class—multiple vector store retrievers are invoked. Each retriever processes the same query independently, leading to redundant embedding computations. This results in unnecessary computational and token overhead, which in turn increases retrieval latency and overall cost.

### Value of Feature

Implementing a caching mechanism in the `BaseEmbedding` class offers a simple and generic solution to eliminate redundant embedding computations, effectively reducing query latency and cost.

linked_prs.title: Adding a very simple implementation of an embeddings cache
linked_prs.body:
# Description

Added a very simple implementation of an embeddings cache that:

- Extends the `BaseEmbedding` class with an `embeddings_cache`, that is a `SimpleKVStore`
- `SimpleKVStore `has now a maximum of data points that can be uploaded to it, to avoid the cache swamping the memory (since the cache is never cleared at runtime). 
-  The clearing of the cache when it overflows the max number of data points (default is 1000) follows a FIFO logic
- If caching is enabled, prior to the embedding we will have a search within the cache: the search within the cache **will not be semantic**, but it will be exact key-value match as the embeddings will be stored with the text to be embedded as the key and the embeddings vector as a the value. If there is a match within the cache, then the corresponding embeddings are returned, else we compute the embeddings, cache them and return them.

Example of a cache:

```json
{
   "embeddings": {
        "text-to-be-embedded": {
              "uuid": [0, 0, 1, 0.3]
         },
        "text-to-be-embedded-2": {
              "uuid": [0, 0, 1, 0.3]
         },
    }
}
```

Fixes #18849
